note: Recast from the English description of Bourguignon & Roisin 2011 (published by Harris 1958 as Schedorhinotermes browni, type locality Gold Ridge, Guadalcanal, Solomon Islands; transferred to Parrhinotermes by Roisin 1988). The measurement abbreviations are expanded into full terms, in millimetres; the soldier measurements are given first for 6 individuals from the type colony, with the range for 39 individuals from 13 colonies in parentheses.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier has the postmentum setose on the upper half only, in contrast to P. barbatus, whose postmentum is setose all over; the measurement ranges of the two overlap, and the key separates them on this character. The alate has a short frons and clypeus (of medium size in P. barbatus), but the measurements of the wings, head and compound eyes also overlap.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head with about 15 setae, posterior margin strongly rounded; frons and clypeus short. Pronotum with about 100 setae. Antenna 17 segments. Measurements (mm; 6 individuals from the same colony): total body length 5.76—6.34; head length (to the apex of the clypeus) 1.04—1.18; head width (including the compound eyes) 1.19—1.26; pronotum length 0.47—0.65, width 0.90—0.95; forewing length 8.34—8.93; compound eye diameter 0.27—0.36.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rectangular, margins slightly rounded, with about 50 small setae and 10 large setae. Labrum long, reaching the apex of the mandibles, its apex forming a rounded brush. Postmentum setose on the upper half only. Antenna 13 segments. Mandibles straight, slightly curved apically, slightly serrate at the base. Measurements (mm; 6 individuals from the type colony, with 39 individuals from 13 colonies in parentheses): head length (to the apex of the clypeus) 1.13—1.19 (1.01—1.33); head length (to the apex of the labrum) 1.56—1.64 (1.40—1.79); maximum head width 0.90—0.94 (0.86—1.05); pronotum width 0.52—0.56 (0.51—0.68); right mandible length 0.69—0.73 (0.64—0.78); maximum postmentum width 0.27—0.31 (0.27—0.34), minimum width 0.16—0.18 (0.16—0.22); hind tibia length 0.75—0.81 (0.70—0.89). Distribution: originally described from the Solomon Islands, common in northern New Guinea and the “Bird's Neck” region; in the regional differentiation with P. barbatus this species is mostly on the northern slopes of New Guinea and P. barbatus on the southern slopes.
